strategy_title: Align BLOCK_M to Actual M to Reduce Wasted Work
strategy_description: When a GEMM tile dimension (BLOCK_M) is hardcoded much larger than the actual problem dimension (e.g., BLOCK_M=16 with M=2), the kernel wastes 87.5% of M-dimension computation on out-of-bounds padding. Reducing BLOCK_M to match the actual M (BLOCK_M=2) cuts executed instructions by ~46% (63K→34K), reduces register pressure from 48 to 34 registers/thread, and improves theoretical occupancy from 62.5% to 75%. The duration dropped from 9.5 µs to 7.01 µs (1.17x speedup) even though the grid size (18 blocks) and achieved occupancy (~6%) remained essentially unchanged, confirming the gain came from eliminating wasted computation rather than improved parallelism.
slow_pseudocode:
@triton.jit
def kernel(...):
    BLOCK_M: tl.constexpr = 16  # M=2 actual → 87.5% of rows are padding
    BLOCK_N: tl.constexpr = 32
    BLOCK_K: tl.constexpr = 32
    # tl.dot computes 16×32×32 tile; only 2×32 rows are valid
    # mask (idx_m < M) guards stores but not the dot computation waste
fast_pseudocode:
@triton.jit
def kernel(...):
    BLOCK_M: tl.constexpr = 2   # matches actual M=2 → zero wasted rows
    BLOCK_N: tl.constexpr = 64  # larger N tile for same grid count
    BLOCK_K: tl.constexpr = 32
    # tl.dot computes 2×64×32 tile; all rows are valid
    # register pressure drops: 48 → 34 registers/thread
    # theoretical occupancy improves: 62.5% → 75%
applicable_when: GEMM kernel where BLOCK_M >> actual M dimension (e.g., BLOCK_M=16 with M=2), causing high wasted computation. Symptoms: executed instructions much higher than expected for problem size, register pressure elevated, theoretical occupancy limited by registers. The fix is purely a constant change with no structural kernel rewrite needed.
do_not_apply_when: BLOCK_M is already close to or smaller than M (no padding waste). Also do not apply when M is large and BLOCK_M is needed for Tensor Core efficiency (tl.dot requires BLOCK_M >= 16 on some backends for MMA; BLOCK_M=2 may fall back to scalar FFMA). Do not combine with ALLOW_TF32=True — prior attempt showed TF32 causes correctness failure (max_diff=257 >> atol=0.001) for this kernel.
framework_notes: In Triton, tl.dot with BLOCK_M=2 may not use Tensor Core MMA on all hardware (MMA typically requires BLOCK_M >= 16). The speedup here came from eliminating wasted scalar FFMA work, not from MMA engagement. BLOCK_N was simultaneously increased from 32 to 64 to maintain the same grid count (18 blocks) while doubling useful work per block in the N dimension.

strategy_title: Halve BLOCK_K to Reduce Shared Memory Bank Conflicts
strategy_description: When the B matrix stride in the K dimension is a multiple of the number of shared memory banks (e.g., stride_bk=1 but stride_bn=96, and 96 mod 32 = 0), loading a [BLOCK_K × BLOCK_N] tile through shared memory causes all threads in a warp to map to the same bank, producing high-way bank conflicts (observed 17-way average, 82% of wavefronts). Halving BLOCK_K from 32 to 16 reduces the number of threads simultaneously issuing conflicting loads per wavefront, cutting average bank conflict ways from 17 to 9 and total bank conflicts from 48384 to 20736. This also halved dynamic shared memory per block (8.7→4.35 KB) and reduced L1/TEX cache throughput from 61.7% to 38.6%, with Warp Cycles Per Issued Instruction dropping from 17.6 to 12.7, yielding a 1.49x speedup despite a modest increase in instruction count (more K-loop iterations).
slow_pseudocode:
# BLOCK_K=32, stride_bn=96, 96 mod 32 = 0 -> 32-way bank conflict potential
BLOCK_K: tl.constexpr = 32
# shared memory tile for B: [32 x BLOCK_N] floats
for k_idx in range(0, K // BLOCK_K):  # 3 iterations for K=96
    b = tl.load(B + (idx_n + 576*idx_m))  # stride-96 access -> bank conflict
    acc += tl.dot(a, b, allow_tf32=False)
fast_pseudocode:
# BLOCK_K=16, same stride_bn=96, but fewer simultaneous conflicting threads
BLOCK_K: tl.constexpr = 16
# shared memory tile for B: [16 x BLOCK_N] floats (half the size)
for k_idx in range(0, K // BLOCK_K):  # 6 iterations for K=96
    b = tl.load(B + (idx_n + 576*idx_m))  # same stride, but fewer threads per wavefront
    acc += tl.dot(a, b, allow_tf32=False)
applicable_when: GEMM kernel where the B matrix stride in the K dimension is a multiple of the shared memory bank count (stride mod 32 == 0 for 32-bank GPUs), causing high-way shared memory bank conflicts (NCU SharedMemoryConflicts rule triggered, bank_conflict_ways >= 8, bank_conflict_wavefronts_pct >= 60%). CPIStall shows MIO (shared memory) stalls as a dominant stall reason (>30% of cycles). L1/TEX Cache Throughput is elevated (>40%) relative to actual compute throughput.
do_not_apply_when: BLOCK_K is already small (<=8) and further reduction would cause tl.dot to fall back to scalar FFMA (losing MMA efficiency). Do not apply when the K dimension is not divisible by the new BLOCK_K (would require masking and break EVEN_K=True). Do not apply when the bank conflict root cause is in the A matrix access pattern rather than B. Also note: this increases the number of K-loop iterations (more loop overhead), which may dominate for very small K values.
framework_notes: In Triton, the shared memory tile size for tl.dot is determined by BLOCK_K × BLOCK_N (for B) and BLOCK_M × BLOCK_K (for A). Reducing BLOCK_K halves the B tile and doubles the number of K-loop iterations. The key insight is that bank conflicts scale with the number of threads simultaneously accessing the same bank per wavefront, which is proportional to BLOCK_K when the stride is a multiple of 32. Also note: this change was bundled with replacing the persistent while-loop (tile_id += NUM_SMS) with a standard pid-based dispatch using GROUP_M reordering; the persistent loop removal may have contributed marginally to the speedup.

strategy_title: BLOCK_M/BLOCK_N Enlargement Explodes Registers, Kills Occupancy
strategy_description: The plan intended to reduce BLOCK_K from 32 to 16 to fix shared memory bank conflicts, but the actual diff also changed BLOCK_M from 2→16 and BLOCK_N from 32→128, which caused registers/thread to explode from 32 to 164 and theoretical occupancy to collapse from 100% to 18.75%. Executed instructions increased 7.7x (22896→175474) because the larger tiles do vastly more work per block without any grid-size increase to compensate. Bank conflicts actually worsened (48384→96768) because the larger BLOCK_N=128 tile generates more shared memory traffic. The root cause of the regression was the unintended tile enlargement, not the BLOCK_K change: when BLOCK_M and BLOCK_N are enlarged beyond the actual problem dimensions (M=2, N=576 with only 18 blocks), register pressure becomes the dominant limiter and theoretical occupancy drops catastrophically.
slow_pseudocode:
# BEFORE: BLOCK_M=2 matches M=2, BLOCK_N=32, BLOCK_K=32, registers=32/thread
@triton.jit
def kernel(...):
    BLOCK_M: tl.constexpr = 2
    BLOCK_N: tl.constexpr = 32
    BLOCK_K: tl.constexpr = 32
    # grid=18, theoretical_occupancy=100%, registers=32/thread
    # bank_conflicts=48384, avg_way=17x
applicable_when: Never: this is a negative experience. Do not enlarge BLOCK_M beyond actual M dimension or enlarge BLOCK_N when the kernel already has low register pressure (32 regs/thread) and 100% theoretical occupancy. Any tile enlargement that pushes registers/thread above ~50 on this kernel will collapse theoretical occupancy below 50%.
do_not_apply_when: Do not revert BLOCK_M from 2 back to 16 when M=2 (actual problem dimension). Do not increase BLOCK_N from 32 to 128 when the kernel already achieves 100% theoretical occupancy with 32 registers/thread — the register explosion from larger tiles will dominate any bank-conflict reduction benefit. Do not add @triton.autotune sweeping only num_warps/num_stages (key=[]) when the grid is already undersized.
framework_notes: In Triton, the accumulator tl.zeros((BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N)) directly determines register allocation. With BLOCK_M=16, BLOCK_N=128, the accumulator alone requires 16*128=2048 float32 values = 2048 registers per warp, far exceeding the hardware limit and forcing register spilling or extreme register pressure (164 regs/thread observed). The Block Limit Registers dropped from 16 to 6 blocks/SM, cutting theoretical occupancy from 100% to 18.75%. The intended BLOCK_K=16 change to fix bank conflicts was correct in isolation but was bundled with the destructive tile enlargement.

strategy_title: Autotune num_warps/num_stages Reduces Smem and Instruction Count
strategy_description: When a kernel already has BLOCK_M matched to the actual M dimension (eliminating wasted computation), adding @triton.autotune sweeping only num_warps and num_stages can still yield meaningful speedup by selecting a lower num_warps configuration that reduces dynamic shared memory per block (8.7 KB → 4.35 KB) and executed instructions (22896 → 17460, ~24% reduction). In this case, the autotune selected num_warps=2 which halved the shared memory footprint and reduced bank conflicts from 48384 to 24192, cutting Warp Cycles Per Issued Instruction from 17.6 to 12.96. This is the inverse of the prior negative experience (exp_001): autotune-only is beneficial when the tile sizes are already correct and the kernel is not grid-underutilized relative to its actual work, but the num_warps selection has a meaningful impact on shared memory pressure.
slow_pseudocode:
# No autotune; fixed num_warps=4 (default), BLOCK_M=2, BLOCK_N=32, BLOCK_K=32
@triton.jit
def kernel(...):
    BLOCK_M: tl.constexpr = 2
    BLOCK_N: tl.constexpr = 32
    BLOCK_K: tl.constexpr = 32
    NUM_SMS: tl.constexpr = 18
    sm_id = tl.program_id(0)
    # persistent tile loop
    tile_id = sm_id
    while tile_id < total_tiles:
        acc = tl.zeros((BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N), dtype=tl.float32)
        for k_idx in range(K // BLOCK_K):
            acc += tl.dot(a, b, allow_tf32=False)
        tl.store(out_ptr, result, mask)
        tile_id += NUM_SMS
# dynamic_smem=8.7KB, bank_conflicts=48384, executed_inst=22896
fast_pseudocode:
# With autotune sweeping num_warps in {2,4}, num_stages in {2,3,4}
@triton.autotune(
    configs=[
        triton.Config({}, num_warps=2, num_stages=2),
        triton.Config({}, num_warps=4, num_stages=2),
        triton.Config({}, num_warps=2, num_stages=3),
        triton.Config({}, num_warps=4, num_stages=3),
        triton.Config({}, num_warps=2, num_stages=4),
        triton.Config({}, num_warps=4, num_stages=4),
    ],
    key=[],
)
@triton.jit
def kernel(...):
    BLOCK_M: tl.constexpr = 2   # unchanged
    BLOCK_N: tl.constexpr = 32  # unchanged
    BLOCK_K: tl.constexpr = 32  # unchanged
    # non-persistent: standard pid-based tile assignment
    pid = tl.program_id(0)
    # GROUP_M reordering, then compute tile
    acc = tl.zeros((BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N), dtype=tl.float32)
    for k_idx in range(K // BLOCK_K):
        acc += tl.dot(a, b, allow_tf32=False)
    tl.store(out_ptr, result, mask)
# dynamic_smem=4.35KB, bank_conflicts=24192, executed_inst=17460
applicable_when: Tile sizes (BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N, BLOCK_K) are already correctly sized to match the actual problem dimensions (no padding waste). The kernel has elevated shared memory bank conflicts and Warp Cycles Per Issued Instruction > 10. num_warps is currently set to a value (e.g., 4) that may be higher than needed, causing excess shared memory allocation. The grid size is fixed and small relative to SM count (grid underutilization is a pre-existing condition, not the target of this optimization).
do_not_apply_when: The primary bottleneck is grid underutilization (waves_per_sm < 0.1) AND tile sizes are not yet optimized — in that regime, autotune-only over num_warps/num_stages cannot fix the root cause and may regress by selecting larger tiles (see exp_001_autotune_num_warps_stages_no_splitk). Also do not apply when the kernel has hardcoded BLOCK_N much larger than needed, as autotune cannot reduce tile sizes it does not control.
framework_notes: In Triton, num_warps controls the number of warps per block, which directly affects the shared memory allocated for the software pipeline (num_stages * num_warps * BLOCK_K * element_size). Reducing num_warps from 4 to 2 halved the dynamic shared memory per block (8.7 KB → 4.35 KB) and halved the bank conflict count (48384 → 24192). The persistent tile loop (while tile_id < total_tiles) was also replaced with a standard pid-based assignment, which may have contributed to the instruction count reduction. The autotune key=[] means the best config is selected once and cached.

strategy_title: Expanding BLOCK_N Doubles Registers, Worsens Bank Conflicts
strategy_description: Changing BLOCK_N from 32 to 64 (while keeping BLOCK_M=2 and BLOCK_K=16) caused registers/thread to nearly double from 36 to 66, dropping theoretical occupancy from 75% to 43.75% and achieved occupancy from 3.12% to 1.56%. Critically, shared memory bank conflicts worsened dramatically: average conflict ways jumped from 9 to 24.7 and the fraction of conflicted wavefronts rose from 66.67% to 94.12%, because the wider BLOCK_N=64 tile generates more simultaneous conflicting accesses per wavefront for the stride-96 B matrix. The autotuner selected block_size=32 (num_warps=1), which halved the thread count per block (64→32 threads), further reducing parallelism. Despite Warp Cycles Per Issued Instruction improving slightly (16.91→12.98), the net effect was a 1.67x slowdown (6.78→13.7 µs) because register pressure and bank conflict degradation dominated.
applicable_when: Never: this is a negative experience. Do not increase BLOCK_N from 32 to 64 for this kernel configuration (BLOCK_M=2, BLOCK_K=16, stride_bn=96). The register explosion and bank conflict amplification dominate any latency-hiding benefit.
do_not_apply_when: Do not increase BLOCK_N when: (1) the B matrix stride is a multiple of 32 (stride_bn mod 32 == 0), as wider tiles amplify bank conflicts rather than reducing them; (2) the kernel is already near the register threshold where a doubling of BLOCK_N pushes registers/thread above ~50, cutting theoretical occupancy below 50%; (3) adding num_warps=1 to the autotune search space risks the autotuner selecting it, which halves thread count per block and further reduces parallelism for an already grid-underutilized kernel.
framework_notes: In Triton, the accumulator tl.zeros((BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N)) scales register usage with BLOCK_N. Going from BLOCK_N=32 to BLOCK_N=64 with BLOCK_M=2 doubles the accumulator from 64 to 128 float32 values per warp, which pushed registers/thread from 36 to 66. The Block Limit Registers dropped from 24 to 28 blocks/SM but Theoretical Active Warps per SM dropped from 48 to 28, cutting theoretical occupancy from 75% to 43.75%. Adding num_warps=1 to the autotune configs is dangerous for tiny-grid kernels: the autotuner selected it, producing block_size=32 (1 warp × 32 threads), which halved the thread count and eliminated any warp-level parallelism for latency hiding.

strategy_title: tl.make_block_ptr Again Fails to Fix Bank Conflicts; Autotune Wins
strategy_description: Replacing manual pointer arithmetic with tl.make_block_ptr + tl.advance (with boundary_check) again produced zero change in SharedMemoryConflicts metrics: bank conflict ways remained at 9, wavefronts conflicted at 66.67%, and L1/TEX hit rate was unchanged at 3.57%. The modest 1.26x speedup (duration 6.78→6.5 µs) is attributable to the expanded autotune config sweep (adding num_warps=1 and num_warps=8 configs) selecting a better num_warps/num_stages combination, not to the block_ptr rewrite itself. The block_ptr change slightly increased register pressure (36→38 regs/thread) and Warp Cycles Per Issued Instruction improved marginally (16.91→15.08), but SharedMemoryConflicts were completely unaffected, confirming that tl.make_block_ptr with order hints cannot resolve bank conflicts caused by strides that are multiples of 32 (stride_bn=96, 96 mod 32=0).
slow_pseudocode:
# Manual pointer arithmetic, BLOCK_K=16, BLOCK_N=64, autotune with 6 configs
# bank_conflicts: 9-way avg, 66.67% wavefronts, duration=6.78us
for k_idx in range(0, K // BLOCK_K):
    xindex = offs_k[None, :] + 96 * offs_a_m[:, None]
    a = tl.load(A + xindex)
    xindex = offs_b_n[None, :] + 576 * offs_k[:, None]
    b = tl.load(B + tl.broadcast_to(...))
    acc += tl.dot(a, b, allow_tf32=False)
fast_pseudocode:
# tl.make_block_ptr + expanded autotune (10 configs incl. num_warps=1,8)
# bank_conflicts: 9-way avg, 66.67% wavefronts (UNCHANGED), duration=6.5us
A_block_ptr = tl.make_block_ptr(
    base=A, shape=(M, K), strides=(stride_am, stride_ak),
    offsets=(pid_m * BLOCK_M, 0), block_shape=(BLOCK_M, BLOCK_K), order=(1, 0)
)
B_block_ptr = tl.make_block_ptr(
    base=B, shape=(K, N), strides=(stride_bk, stride_bn),
    offsets=(0, pid_n * BLOCK_N), block_shape=(BLOCK_K, BLOCK_N), order=(0, 1)
)
for k_idx in range(0, K // BLOCK_K):
    a = tl.load(A_block_ptr, boundary_check=(0, 1), padding_option='zero')
    b = tl.load(B_block_ptr, boundary_check=(0, 1), padding_option='zero')
    acc += tl.dot(a, b, allow_tf32=False)
    A_block_ptr = tl.advance(A_block_ptr, (0, BLOCK_K))
    B_block_ptr = tl.advance(B_block_ptr, (BLOCK_K, 0))
applicable_when: Never: tl.make_block_ptr with order hints does not eliminate shared memory bank conflicts when the matrix stride is a multiple of the bank count (stride mod 32 == 0). This has now been confirmed ineffective across three separate iterations (exp_003, exp_004, exp_005) with different BLOCK_K, BLOCK_N, and autotune configurations.
do_not_apply_when: Do not use tl.make_block_ptr + order hints as a strategy for fixing SharedMemoryConflicts when the root cause is a stride that is a multiple of 32 (e.g., stride_bn=96). The swizzle engine does not override the physical bank mapping determined by the global memory stride. Additionally, boundary_check=(0,1) adds register pressure overhead (observed +2 regs/thread consistently). Any speedup observed when bundling this change with an expanded autotune config sweep is attributable to the autotune selection, not the block_ptr rewrite.
framework_notes: In Triton, tl.make_block_ptr with order=(1,0) or order=(0,1) hints at the preferred memory layout for the swizzle engine, but this only affects how data is staged into shared memory from global memory — it cannot change the bank conflict pattern when the conflict arises from the global memory stride mapping directly to shared memory banks. For stride_bn=96 (96 mod 32 = 0), every warp's access to the B tile maps all threads to the same bank regardless of block pointer construction. The boundary_check parameter adds extra predicate instructions that inflate register usage by ~2 registers/thread.

strategy_title: tl.make_block_ptr + USE_FAST_ACCUM Reduces Stalls but Raises Registers
strategy_description: Replacing manual index arithmetic loads with tl.make_block_ptr (removing boundary_check) and enabling USE_FAST_ACCUM=True reduced executed instructions by ~29% (16488→11736) and cut Warp Cycles Per Issued Instruction from 16.9 to 13.2, reducing L1TEX stall cycles from 10.3 to 7.9 per warp. However, registers/thread increased substantially (36→60), which halved the block size from 64 to 32 threads and dropped theoretical occupancy from 75% to 50%, partially offsetting the per-warp efficiency gains. The net result was a modest 1.14x speedup despite the instruction count reduction, because the register pressure increase from tl.make_block_ptr's internal state variables consumed the register budget freed by removing boundary checks.
slow_pseudocode:
# Manual index arithmetic loads with boundary_check, USE_FAST_ACCUM=False
USE_FAST_ACCUM: tl.constexpr = False
for k_idx in range(0, tl.cdiv(K, BLOCK_K)):
    a_k_idx_vals = offs_k[None, :] + (k_idx * BLOCK_K)
    xindex = a_k_idx_vals + 96 * offs_a_m[:, None]
    a = tl.load(A + xindex)
    b_k_idx_vals = offs_k[:, None] + (k_idx * BLOCK_K)
    xindex = offs_b_n[None, :] + 576 * b_k_idx_vals
    b = tl.load(B + tl.broadcast_to(b_k_idx_vals + 96*offs_b_n[None, :], [BLOCK_K, BLOCK_N]))
    acc += tl.dot(a, b, allow_tf32=ALLOW_TF32, out_dtype=ACC_TYPE)
tl.store(out_ptr + ..., tmp16, mask)
# registers=36/thread, block_size=64, executed_inst=16488
fast_pseudocode:
# tl.make_block_ptr with no boundary_check, USE_FAST_ACCUM=True
USE_FAST_ACCUM: tl.constexpr = True
A_block_ptr = tl.make_block_ptr(
    base=A, shape=(M, K), strides=(stride_am, stride_ak),
    offsets=(pid_m * BLOCK_M, 0), block_shape=(BLOCK_M, BLOCK_K), order=(1, 0)
)
B_block_ptr = tl.make_block_ptr(
    base=B, shape=(K, N), strides=(stride_bk, stride_bn),
    offsets=(0, pid_n * BLOCK_N), block_shape=(BLOCK_K, BLOCK_N), order=(0, 1)
)
for k_idx in range(0, tl.cdiv(K, BLOCK_K)):
    a = tl.load(A_block_ptr)  # no boundary_check
    b = tl.load(B_block_ptr)  # no boundary_check
    acc = tl.dot(a, b, acc, allow_tf32=ALLOW_TF32, out_dtype=ACC_TYPE)  # fast accum form
    A_block_ptr = tl.advance(A_block_ptr, (0, BLOCK_K))
    B_block_ptr = tl.advance(B_block_ptr, (BLOCK_K, 0))
tl.store(out_ptr + ..., tmp16)  # no mask
# registers=60/thread, block_size=32, executed_inst=11736
applicable_when: GEMM kernel with manual index arithmetic loads (computing xindex = offset + stride * k_idx per iteration) where all tile boundaries are exactly divisible (M%BLOCK_M==0, K%BLOCK_K==0, N%BLOCK_N==0), so boundary_check is provably unnecessary. CPIStall shows L1TEX stalls as dominant (>50% of cycles). Current register pressure is low-to-moderate (≤40 regs/thread) so that the block_ptr state overhead (~24 additional registers) will not collapse theoretical occupancy below 50%.
do_not_apply_when: Registers/thread are already elevated (>40) before the change — tl.make_block_ptr introduces significant register overhead for its internal pointer state, which can push registers from 36 to 60+, halving block size and theoretical occupancy. Do not apply when the grid is severely undersized (waves_per_sm < 0.01) and occupancy is already the primary bottleneck — the register increase will worsen occupancy further. Also do not remove boundary_check when tile dimensions do not exactly divide problem dimensions (would produce incorrect results).
framework_notes: In Triton, tl.make_block_ptr creates a block pointer object that internally tracks base address, shape, strides, offsets, and block shape — this state is stored in registers, adding ~24 registers/thread overhead compared to manual index arithmetic. The 3-argument form of tl.dot (tl.dot(a, b, acc, ...)) enables USE_FAST_ACCUM which uses a faster accumulation path on Tensor Cores. Removing boundary_check=(0,1) from tl.load on a block_ptr eliminates per-element masking instructions but does NOT reduce register pressure — the block_ptr state itself is the dominant register consumer. The autotune config expansion (adding num_warps=1 configs) selected num_warps=1 (block_size=32) as the winner, which contributed to the occupancy drop.

strategy_title: Doubling BLOCK_N Improves IPC But Increases Duration
strategy_description: Increasing BLOCK_N from 32 to 64 in a tiny GEMM kernel (M=2, N=576, K=96) doubled the work per block, improving Warp Cycles Per Issued Instruction from 16.91 to 11.25 and L2 Hit Rate from 32% to 46%, while reducing shared memory bank conflict ways from 9 to 6.5. However, the elapsed cycles increased from 10142 to 11092 and registers/thread grew from 36 to 44, reducing theoretical occupancy from 75% to 62.5%. The net speedup of 1.10x is modest and primarily driven by better instruction efficiency per warp rather than improved parallelism, since the grid remained at 18 blocks on 132 SMs (0.01 waves/SM) in both cases — the autotune selected BLOCK_N=64 but the grid was not halved as intended, suggesting the dynamic grid lambda may not have been applied correctly.
fast_pseudocode:
# BLOCK_N=64 hardcoded, grid=(18,1,1) unchanged
@triton.autotune(configs=[Config({}, num_warps=2, num_stages=1), Config({}, num_warps=8, num_stages=4), ...], key=[])
@triton.jit
def kernel(...):
    BLOCK_N: tl.constexpr = 64
    BLOCK_M: tl.constexpr = 2
    BLOCK_K: tl.constexpr = 16
    # 18 blocks, each processes [2x64] output tile (2x work per block)
    # Warp Cycles Per Issued Instruction = 11.25
    # L2 Hit Rate = 46%
    # registers/thread: 36 -> 44, theoretical occupancy: 75% -> 62.5%
applicable_when: Tiny GEMM kernel where BLOCK_N is smaller than the N dimension and IssueSlotUtilization is flagged (scheduler No Eligible > 90%). Warp Cycles Per Issued Instruction is high (>12) and L2 Hit Rate is low (<40%), suggesting the working set fits in L2 with a larger tile. The kernel has low register pressure (< 40 regs/thread) leaving headroom for BLOCK_N enlargement without catastrophic occupancy loss.
do_not_apply_when: Register pressure is already near the block-limit threshold (>40 regs/thread) — BLOCK_N enlargement will push registers higher and reduce theoretical occupancy. Do not apply when BLOCK_N enlargement is combined with TF32 (see exp_002_tf32_only_regression). Do not apply when the grid is already severely undersized and the goal is to halve the grid further — if the dynamic grid lambda is not correctly updated at the call site, the grid will remain unchanged and the larger tile will simply do redundant work. The speedup ceiling is low (~10%) for kernels that are fundamentally latency-dominated with < 0.01 waves/SM.
framework_notes: In Triton, changing BLOCK_N as a hardcoded constexpr (rather than promoting it to an autotune parameter) means the grid lambda at the call site must be manually updated to reflect the new tile count. If the grid remains fixed at the old value (e.g., 18 blocks for BLOCK_N=32) after changing to BLOCK_N=64, each block will process a [2x64] tile but the grid will cover 18*64=1152 N-elements instead of 576, causing out-of-bounds accesses or redundant computation (masked by boundary checks). The profiling shows grid_size=18 unchanged in both before and after, suggesting the grid lambda was not updated — yet the kernel still produced a speedup, likely because the boundary mask (idx_n < N) correctly suppressed out-of-bounds stores and the larger tile improved L2 reuse for valid elements.
